title: Lay a Japanese set meal for the guest opposite: rice left, soup right, fish head left
keywords: laying a place for a guest opposite
instruction: Set this teishoku tray for the guest who sits on the indigo cushion across the table, facing you. The white bowl is rice, the black lacquer bowl is miso soup, the small blue bowl is the side dish, and the plate holds a whole grilled fish. Put all four on the tray the way a Japanese set meal is laid for the guest, then let go.
context: Japanese set meals (teishoku) are laid on the tray to a standard layout, given in the washoku guidance of Japan's Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries and in table-manner and school food-education material: seen by the diner, rice front left, soup front right, the main dish back right and the side dish back left (the ichiju-nisai form), and a whole fish with its head to the diner's left and its belly toward the diner. Restaurant servers, ryokan inn staff and hospital and care-home meal-service workers lay trays this way at every meal. The tray is laid for the guest, who sits opposite and faces the server, so the layout has to be read from the guest's side: laid from the server's own side, every dish lands in the opposite place and the fish faces the wrong way. Here the meal is at about two thirds of real size, the robot is the server, and nothing on the tray marks where anything goes.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A Japanese set meal at about 2:3 scale; eight things are on the table, all but the four dishes fixed to it. (1) Meal tray: a flat dark red lacquered wooden board, 220 mm (x) by 300 mm (y), 6 mm thick, at x 22.0 to 44.0 cm, y -15.0 to +15.0 cm; its centre lines are x 33.0 cm and y 0. (2) Guest's cushion: a flat indigo fabric cushion, 120 mm (x) by 200 mm (y), 2 mm thick, beyond the tray's far edge at x 45.5 to 57.5 cm, y -10.0 to +10.0 cm. The guest sits on it facing the robot (facing -x), so the guest's left is -y. (3, 4) Serving boards: two light wood boards, 245 mm (x) by 110 mm (y), 2 mm thick, at x 16.0 to 40.5 cm, one at y +24.5 to +35.5 cm (left) and one at y -35.5 to -24.5 cm (right). The four dishes are loose, each one rigid piece, standing on the serving boards: (5) Rice bowl: a cream-white glazed porcelain bowl, straight-sided (a cylinder 66 mm across and 44 mm tall), filled level with light foam under a 54 mm disc of white rice replica 1 mm proud of its rim (45 mm tall in all), 80 g in all, on the right board centred at x 33.0 cm, y -30.0 cm. (6) Side-dish bowl: a blue glazed porcelain bowl, straight-sided (a cylinder 55 mm across and 34 mm tall), filled level with foam under a 44 mm disc of green vegetable replica 1 mm proud (35 mm in all), 50 g in all, on the right board centred at x 21.5 cm, y -30.0 cm. (7) Soup bowl: a black lacquered wooden bowl, straight-sided (a cylinder 64 mm across and 45 mm tall) with a red lacquered rim band of the same width and 4 mm tall on top of that, filled with foam under a 52 mm disc of brown miso replica 1 mm proud of the rim (50 mm in all), 70 g in all, on the left board centred at x 20.5 cm, y +30.0 cm. (8) Fish plate: a white glazed rectangular plate (melamine, or a white lacquered wooden slab), 130 by 60 mm and 12 mm thick with straight edges, with a painted resin replica of a whole grilled fish glued along its middle: a grey-brown body 80 by 35 mm and 18 mm tall, a dark head 20 by 28 mm and 16 mm tall at one end, a dark tail fin 10 by 24 by 4 mm at the other, a white belly strip 70 by 8 mm along one long edge of its top and a dark dorsal ridge 60 by 8 by 3 mm along the other (the fish 110 by 35 mm and 21 mm tall; plate and fish 120 g together). It lies on the left board centred at x 33.0 cm, y +30.0 cm, its length along x, the fish's head toward +x (away from the robot) and its belly toward +y. The bowls stand upright. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last control step from the four dishes' poses (in a real trial: a top photo before the arms move away, for the let-go rule, then a ruler once they have); the simulator also gives each gripper's pad-tip point (midway between its finger tips) and how far it is open. The guest sits beyond the tray's far edge facing the robot, so the guest's left is -y (the robot's right) and the guest's front is the tray's far half. The tray's centre lines (x 33.0 cm, y 0) split it into quadrants seen from the guest: front left (x above 33.0 cm, y below 0), front right (x above 33.0 cm, y above 0), back left (x below 33.0 cm, y below 0) and back right (x below 33.0 cm, y above 0). A dish is placed when all of these hold: its centre (the middle of its base) is in its quadrant, at least 10 mm from both centre lines; its footprint (a bowl's base circle, the plate's 130 x 60 mm outline) sticks out past the tray's edge by at most 5 mm; it stands on the tray (its lowest point within 3 mm of the tray top, not on another dish or held up); it is upright (tilted at most 10 degrees); it is let go (no gripper's pad-tip point is less than 10 mm above the dish's top while within that gripper's finger reach of its footprint seen from above: 65 mm fully open, 52 mm closed on the rice bowl, over every yaw); and it is still (its centre moved under 3 mm in all over the last 1 s). The quadrants, as the basic washoku layout puts them for the guest: rice bowl front left, soup bowl front right, fish plate back right, side-dish bowl back left. The fish plate also needs the fish's head pointing within 15 degrees of the guest's left (-y) and its belly within 15 degrees of the guest (+x), seen from above. Each placed dish earns 0.25, except that two dishes whose footprints cross by more than 1 mm both earn 0 (one on, leaning on or pushed under another), and a dish that tilted past 45 degrees at any step of the trial (tipped, its food spilled) earns 0 for the rest of the trial, even if set upright again. Score = the sum: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or 1.0. Every outcome: the full layout for the guest, 1.0; the same with the fish's head to the guest's right (+y) or the plate lying front to back, 0.75; the soup tipped on the way and set upright in its place, 0.75; rice and side dish swapped front to back, 0.5; the rice bowl pushed against the side dish so their footprints cross, 0.5; one arm's two dishes left on their board, 0.5; only the fish right, 0.25; the layout laid from the robot's own side (rice near on the robot's left, soup near on its right, fish far on its right with the head to the robot's left, side dish far on its left), 0: every dish is in the opposite quadrant. A dish still held, astride a centre line, hanging off the tray or on the table earns 0 itself. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 2.5 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at about two thirds of real size with the simulator's default friction: each bowl is a solid cylinder with a disc of food on top (nothing hollow, no liquid), and the fish is a rigid replica glued to its plate. No chopsticks, soup lid or pickles; the guest is shown only by the cushion. The rule, which quadrant each dish takes and which way the fish lies seen from the guest, is kept exactly. The grippers are read only to check that each dish was let go.
reset_notes: Stand the rice bowl back upright on the right serving board centred at x 33.0 cm, y -30.0 cm and the side-dish bowl at x 21.5 cm, y -30.0 cm; the soup bowl upright on the left board centred at x 20.5 cm, y +30.0 cm; lay the fish plate on the left board centred at x 33.0 cm, y +30.0 cm, its length along x, the fish's head toward +x and its belly toward +y. The tray, cushion and boards are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
